news.title: Grasim Industries’ net profit declines 35% to ₹1,029.42 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Grasim Industries recorded a 34.7 percent decline in net consolidated profit for Q2 FY27. The company's total income, however, increased by 25.3 percent in the same period. Revenue from the building materials business also saw growth, driven by improved profitability in cement. Additionally, Birla Opus and Birla Pivot both reported significant revenue increases in Q2 FY27. The company's investment in the Canadian joint venture further reflects its growth strategy.

news.title: TARC posts profit of ₹4.39 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: TARC Ltd has announced a consolidated net profit of Rs 4.39 crore for the quarter ended September. This is a significant improvement from a net loss of Rs 15.76 crore reported last year. Total income increased to Rs 134.06 crore from Rs 34.10 crore during the same period. The company achieved sales bookings of Rs 955 crore in the first half of this fiscal year.

news.title: Shriram Properties’ net profit jumps 152% to ₹21.59 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: In Q2 FY27, Shriram Properties posted a spectacular 151.9 percent growth in net profit compared to the last fiscal year, with total income climbing to ₹272.25 crore. The firm achieved record collections of ₹795 crore in the first half of FY27 and further solidified its position by acquiring more equity in four joint ventures, while ambitiously working to double its project portfolio.

news.title: Consumer commission orders Livspace to pay ₹87.16 lakh; cites unsafe work and inferior materials
news.para: Livspace India Pvt Ltd has been held responsible for unsafe renovation work in a Goregaon flat. The Maharashtra State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the company guilty of poor workmanship and negligence. Deepak Ruiya, the complainant, reported serious safety hazards such as exposed live wires and a collapsing kitchen shutter. Following an incomplete project, the commission ordered Livspace to refund Rs 87 lakh to Ruiya.

news.title: Mumbai police order first eviction under Maharashtra Rent Control Act
news.para: City police have completed their first eviction under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, returning a flat to its owners. The owners claimed that tenants did not vacate their flat after their leave-and-licence agreement expired. The eviction proceedings were initiated, and the tenants were ordered to pay compensation for the delay. The government is addressing the backlog of rent-related cases in Mumbai with this new approach.

news.title: Godrej Properties acquires 31-acre land in Indore for plotted housing project
news.para: Godrej Properties has acquired around 31 acres of land for developing a residential project in Indore. The new project will offer a saleable area of approximately 0.7 million sq ft and contain various residential plots. This acquisition represents the company's third project in Indore, following the ongoing development of two existing projects.

news.title: West Bengal CM sets November 30 deadline for ineligible housing beneficiaries to return funds, orders CID probe
news.para: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has set a deadline of November 30 for ineligible beneficiaries to return funds as part of a crackdown on irregularities. This comes alongside a CID investigation into 57,000 potentially fictitious beneficiaries involved in a rural housing scheme. To ensure accountability, a special investigation team will oversee the process.

news.title: UP-RERA bars blanket consent from homebuyers for changes in building plans
news.para: Before making any significant changes to a project, promoters need to clearly inform buyers about how these changes will affect the carpet area, common areas, and overall project specifications in writing. Additionally, for any major alterations to the approved plans, they must get the written consent of at least two-thirds of the allottees involved.

news.title: HERC orders builder to apply for electrification plan of BPTP Park under single-point supply regime in 30 days
news.para: Residents of BPTP Park 81 can expect to receive uninterrupted electricity connections after a regulatory decision. The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission permitted the retention of the existing power distribution network rather than requiring a complete overhaul. Additionally, Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam must release pending connections following technical and safety procedures. BPTP is required to complete necessary upgrades to meet approved electrical load requirements.

news.title: GRAP-3 restrictions: Noida administration directs strict ban on construction activities
news.para: The Gautam Buddh Nagar administration has mandated a strict ban on construction activities to address air pollution. District Magistrate Medha Roopam emphasized the need for action against violators during a review meeting. Various departments are required to monitor compliance and conduct regular inspections effectively. The Air Quality Index in Noida has reached alarming levels, indicating very poor air conditions.

news.title: DTCP removes diesel generator sets from green areas in Gurugram's Suncity
news.para: The Department of Town and Country Planning intervened to eliminate four diesel generators that were improperly positioned in a green belt of Suncity township. After multiple local complaints, the DTCP warned the residents' association. While four units were dismantled, a larger generator continues to operate, with its owner now facing a strict 48-hour deadline to comply or risk legal action.

news.title: DTCP seals four buildings in DLF-2, resumes crackdown on illegal commercial use
news.para: In DLF Phase 2, the DTCP has reinitiated its sealing efforts aimed at unauthorized commercial usages. Four properties, which included three guest houses and one office, were sealed due to non-compliance with land-use regulations. This enforcement drive follows an earlier operation on October 12 in Sushant Lok-1 and seeks to curb unlawful commercial activities in residential zones.

news.title: Telangana housing board auctions plot for ₹2.18 lakh per sq yard
news.para: The Telangana Housing Board held a highly successful auction, selling 11 of the 21 land parcels in Kukatpally. With bids ranging from ₹1.56 lakh to ₹2.18 lakh per square yard, the event attracted 23 eager participants. The total revenue generated from this auction reached an impressive ₹33.11 crore. This initiative highlights the board's commitment to efficiently utilizing vacant land assets.

news.title: Building approvals hit digi roadblocks as Tamil Nadu rules await portal update
news.para: Builders in Chennai are facing significant delays in securing building approvals due to outdated software. The government has introduced regulatory relaxations, but these changes are not yet reflected online. Technical issues with the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority’s portal are also causing application stalls. Developers are experiencing persistent problems at nearly every stage of the approval process.

news.title: Tamil Nadu CM approves ₹1,401 crore housing project to build 6,157 tenements in Chennai
news.para: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has given the go-ahead for the construction of 6,157 housing units in Chennai aimed at supporting underprivileged residents. These projects, located in nine different areas, will offer modern infrastructure and essential amenities. Furthermore, a special interest waiver scheme will benefit 6,496 Tamil Nadu Housing Board allottees in managing their arrears.

news.title: Home sales in USA slumps 8.8% in October, slowest in more than 16 years as mortgage rates surged
news.para: October witnessed a significant drop in sales of previously occupied homes across the U.S., largely due to rising mortgage interest rates. The annual sales volume experienced a 5.5% decline from September, marking the lowest rate since 2010. Nevertheless, home prices rose to a median of $416,700, and the supply of unsold homes grew, hinting at a more balanced market.

news.title: ED files prosecution complaint against ADEL Landmarks, 40 others in homebuyer fraud case
news.para: The Enforcement Directorate alleged that ADEL Landmarks collected about ₹1,075 crore as booking advances from 4,771 buyers across residential projects in Gurugram, Faridabad and Palwal. The agency has also attached properties, including land parcels, measuring around 340 acres and valued at ₹585.46 crore.

news.title: Three Ansal group directors arrested over ₹77.66 crore RERA dues in Greater Noida
news.para: Three directors of the Ansal group were arrested for not clearing substantial dues to the Real Estate Regulatory Authority. They owed over Rs 77.66 crore in land revenue, which has led to legal action. After an arrest warrant was issued, they were detained for up to 15 days. The district administration emphasized the importance of recovering outstanding dues through strict legal measures.

news.title: Odisha RERA grants four-month relief to housing projects hit by West Asia conflict
news.para: Odisha Real Estate Regulatory Authority has announced a four-month extension for project timelines affected by the West Asia conflict. This decision follows an advisory from the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs regarding project completion dates. Promoters are not required to pay any fees to obtain this extension. Registered projects with completion dates on or after February 28, 2026, qualify for this relief.

news.title: Spain approves housing measures after huge protests
news.para: In response to widespread public unrest and a significant general strike, Spain's interim lower house of parliament has officially approved housing reforms aimed at limiting evictions and controlling real estate speculation. These measures are set against the backdrop of upcoming national elections on November 29, where the opposition, led by the Popular Party, has signalled intentions to repeal such reforms if they come to power.
